LC 242 · Valid Anagram · Easy

Given two strings `s` and `t`, return `true` if `t` is an anagram of `s`, and `false` otherwise.

questions.question: Which approach and high-level steps fit this problem?
options: Sort each string as a key into a hash map of lists; return the groups.
Sliding window across the whole list of strings.
Binary search each string.
Two pointers comparing only first and last string.
questions.explanation: Group by a canonical key (sorted letters or count tuple).

LC 49 · Group Anagrams · Medium

Given an array of strings `strs`, group the anagrams together. You can return the answer in any order. An Anagram is a word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of a different word or phrase, typically using all the original letters exactly once.

Hash map of all substrings first (required).
Stack of characters only.
Two pointers from ends ignoring the middle.

questions.question: Which approach and high-level steps fit this problem?
options: Sliding window with need/have counts: expand right; shrink left while valid; track minimum covering window.

Stack matching every letter in t.
questions.explanation: Minimum covering substring = window that stays valid while you shrink.

LC 76 · Minimum Window Substring · Hard

Given two strings `s` and `t`, return the minimum window in `s` which will contain all the characters in `t`. If there is no such window in `s` that covers all characters in `t`, return the empty string `""`. Note that If there is such a window, it is guaranteed that there will always be only one unique minimum window in `s`.
